title: Terraform module: VPC KMS proxy & Vault integration for HSM-backed secrets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that deploys a VPC-scoped KMS proxy and Vault integration layer enabling HSM-backed key usage for Redwood Private. The module should support multiple cloud KMS endpoints and on-prem HSM gateways, provide configurable network ACLs, health checks, secret rotation orchestration hooks (for Secrets Manager and Vault), and safe upgrade paths for key metadata without disrupting active secrets. Target consumers: Private deployment engineers and customer on-prem packages.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes inputs/outputs and example usage for AWS VPC and GCP VPC installs
KMS proxy (containerized) can be deployed in customer VPC subnets with IAM/bindings and security groups configured by module
Vault transit integration is automated: Vault has a mount configured that routes to underlying HSM via the proxy
Secrets rotation job template is provided (Kubernetes CronJob + sample Terraform job) to rotate secrets using HSM keys
Health check endpoints (prometheus metrics + /healthz) provided and module wires a monitoring target for Console ingestion
Rolling upgrade strategy documented and tested: proxy upgrade with sticky connection draining without Vault downtime
Module has unit/integration tests in CI and a sample deployment that runs in an e2e environment
Security review checklist items completed and documented in design doc
design_notes: Architecture: Module deploys a small proxy service (containerized) with sidecar TLS termination where needed. Proxy holds persistent, minimal state: routing table to HSM, auth creds stored in KMS/Vault sealed storage.
Trade-offs: We avoid directly exposing HSM endpoints to multiple tenants; proxy centralizes session and connection pooling which reduces HSM session churn at cost of single-process complexity.
Compatibility: Support AWS KMS Custom Key Store (CKS), CloudHSM, and PKCS#11-based on-prem HSM via gateway. For customers without HSM, module can operate in KMS-only mode.
Network controls: Module exposes variables for public/private subnets, NACLs, and optional NAT egress. By default, proxies are deployed in private subnets with no inbound internet access.
Secret rotation: Provide a template pattern where a rotation job calls Vault rewrap/rotate APIs or triggers AWS Secrets Manager rotation lambdas while validating new key references before cutover.
Observability: Expose metrics for connection health, latency to HSM, and rotation success rate. Include Prometheus scrape_config snippet in examples.
Upgrade path: Use blue/green container rollout for proxy with connection draining. Keep a migration tool for key metadata changes to avoid re-wrapping all secrets during small key policy updates.

Failure modes: If proxy becomes unhealthy, automatic fallback policy routes Vault operations to a pre-configured soft-fail KMS path (non-HSM) to avoid total secret unavailability; documented as customer-configurable and gated behind explicit opt-in.

risks: HSM session limits could be exceeded if pooling defaults are conservative; need stress testing with emulator before GA.
Incorrect upgrade could cause Vault transit operations to fail; rollback plan must be tested end-to-end.
Customer network misconfiguration (NACLs/route tables) may block HSM traffic; provide validation script in module outputs.
